newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Job, money before marriage, say young Singaporeans.
newsitem.headline: Job, money before marriage, say young Singaporeans.

text.p: Marriage is low on the list of priorities for young Singaporeans, a survey has found.
The daily Straits Times newspaper said on Monday that among graduates aged 21 to 36, marriage was the fourth most important goal in the next five years, after career, finance and a house.
Marriage came fifth after the same three goals and education for non-graduates and undergraduates aged 18 to 29.
The Straits Times was quoting a survey by Singapore's Social Development Unit in 1996 that covered 815 undergraduates and 1,000 working adults.
The survey did find that majorities in each category would prefer marriage to being single, but there was a sharp difference among men and women as to the importance of a suitable partner.
Among women, 48 percent said they would prefer to stay single rather than lower their expectations or seek help from matchmakers.
Among men, only 37 percent took that view.
